title: Registry pin validation playbook — multi-region scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a practical, operational playbook for validating model registry version pins and their interaction with routing rules across multiple regions and control-plane decisions. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and release owners who perform rollouts, emergency pin changes, and cross-region failovers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated clusters managed by Redwood control plane. Private deployments may adapt the same checks but may require different telemetry hooks.
- Covers: pin creation & validation, pre-rollout checks, compatibility scoring, routing policy interactions (affinity, priority, fallback), and operational checks during failover/cutover.
- Assumes models in the registry have metadata: model_id, version, architecture, quantization_profile, supported_kv_cache_format, max_context_tokens, compatible_inference_kernels (list), region_constraints (optional), and rollout_tag (canary|stable).

High-level problem statement:
When a tenant or platform flow pins a model version (explicit version binding), the control plane must ensure routability without violating latency SLOs or breaking compatibility with serving runtime across regions. Pins can cause requests that previously routed to a compatible variant to be forced to a region or node type where the pinned variant is unsupported (different kernel, incompatible quantization, or missing accelerators). We need deterministic validation and scoring to prevent degraded traffic or silent failures.

Definitions / glossary (short):
- Pin: explicit model version binding at registry or route level.
- Variant: runtime-optimized build of the same model (quantized/float16/2-bit).
- Routing policy: set of rules (region affinity, cost-preference, latency-preference, fallback-order).
- Compatibility score: numeric heuristic used by control plane to decide if route->version is safe.

Compatibility scoring (recommended heuristic):
- Base score = 100. Subtract penalties:
  - architecture_mismatch: -100 (hard fail)
  - kernel_support_missing_in_region: -60
  - quant_profile_mismatch: -30
  - kv_cache_format_mismatch: -20
  - estimated_latency_increase_pct > 30%: -25
  - memory_exceed_node: -100 (hard fail)
  - region_constraint_violation: -100
- Thresholds: 
  - score >= 70: green (allowed, no changes)
  - 40 <= score < 70: amber (allowed with warnings, recommend canary)
  - score < 40 or any hard fail: red (block pin until remediation)

Notes on signals used by scoring:
- Runtime capability catalog (per-region): list of supported kernels, accelerator types, memory profiles, and quantization paths.
- Historical latency model per model-version-region pair: expected p50/p95 for typical sequence lengths.
- Telemetry of previous region microfailures (e.g., new kernel OOMs).
- Customer-tier policy: enterprise tenants may allow amber if SLA approved.

Pre-pin validation checklist (automatable):
1) Registry metadata completeness: model/version entries must include quant_profile, kernel_hashes, max_tokens, and supported_kv_cache_format.
2) Control-plane lookup: fetch runtime capability catalog for all candidate regions.
3) Run compatibility scoring for each region under every active routing policy that could route traffic to the pin (including cross-region fallback paths).
4) Flag any hard-fail region as non-routable and remove from candidate sets; surface to owner with remediation steps.
5) If any active region becomes amber, create automated canary policy suggestion (e.g., 5% of traffic to amber region for 24h).
6) Estimate unit-cost delta per token per region and attach to approval metadata.
7) Create an audit entry in registry with pre-pin validation snapshot (score breakdown per-region).

Routing policy interactions to consider:
- Region affinity + pin: pins reduce routing flexibility. The control plane should compute "effective routing entropy" after pinning and warn if entropy falls below a safe threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 independent capacity pools).
- Fallback orders: if primary region lacks support, ensure fallback region supports the pinned build; otherwise, fallback must trigger automatic variant substitution (only if allowed by pin scope) or failover to previous pinned version.
- Cost-priority routing: if pin forces traffic to more expensive regions/providers, add billing-owner approval.
- Canary & canary-to-stable transitions: when routing policies include percentage-based canaries across regions, ensure pinned version is rolled out with region-aware canary sequencing to detect regional regressions.

Operational playbook — common scenarios:
1) New pin request (normal rollout):
   - Trigger pre-pin validation (automated).
   - If all green: allow pin and schedule immediate rollout or scheduled rollout per SLA.
   - If amber: suggest canary policy and require explicit approval for amber zones.
   - If red: block and list remediation (build variant with supported kernel, adjust quant profile, add region-specific variant).

2) Emergency pin (hotfix):
   - Short-circuit full scoring but still run hard-fail checks (memory, arch, region constraints).
   - If any hard fail: reject and notify on-call with remediation steps.
   - If amber or green: allow pin but attach automatic 30-minute elevated monitoring and rollback window.

3) Cross-region failover (region outage):
   - Control plane computes which pinned versions are candidate for automatic reroute. Apply compatibility scoring on-the-fly for potential target regions.
   - If none meet green: apply queued fallback policy (variant substitution or degrade to read-only if applicable) and fire SRE incident.

4) Variant substitution vs strict pin semantics:
   - Registry-level pin type: strict vs flexible. Strict pins require exact version routing and cannot be substituted; flexible pins permit control plane to pick compatible variant builds (e.g., same model+version but different quant).
   - Default policy: pins created by customers are strict unless explicitly set flexible. Internal platform pins may be flexible to preserve availability.

Telemetry and dashboards to build (recommended):
- "Pin impact" dashboard: shows for each pin the number of regions passing/amber/failing, expected latency delta, and effective capacity pools remaining.
- Pre-pin audit log: searchable by pin id, owner, and date.
- Canary regressions view: show evals, token-level cost, p50/p95 changes for canary vs stable per region.
- Alerts: pin-caused routing entropy drop, pin-induced memory OOMs in 1 minute window, sudden cost increase >20% tied to pin.

Suggested API flows and control-plane hooks:
- POST /pins/validate (input: model_id, version, pin_scope {tenant, route, global}, routing_policy_ids): returns per-region compatibility scores, suggested canary policy, and cost delta estimate.
- POST /pins (input includes validate=true): performs validation and, if green/approved, creates pin and audit snapshot.
- webhook: /controlplane/pin-events -> triggers rollout orchestrator and alerting channels.

Runbook excerpts (quick steps for on-call):
- When alert "pin-routing-entropy-drop" fires: 1) check the pre-pin audit; 2) examine region health and kernel errors in logs; 3) if pin is recent (<24h) consider immediate rollback to previous pin; 4) if rollback not possible, switch to flexible fallback rule for affected tenant.
- When we see "canary-latency-regression" in a region: 1) pause canary progression; 2) route canary traffic away from region; 3) collect model eval traces and failure rates; 4) coordinate with build-owner to produce compatible variant.

Remediation playbook samples (developer actions):
- If quant_profile_mismatch: rebuild quantized variant for the missing quant profile or enable compatible kernel shim in region (longer).
- If kernel_support_missing: add kernel build to runtime images for that region and mark when available; until then mark region as non-routable.
- If memory exceed: produce a trimmed model (smaller context size) or enable shard serving if supported.

Open questions & followups (for roadmap):
- Should the control plane automatically produce a region-specific variant when a pin fails compatibility (cost/time tradeoffs)?
- How tightly should tenant-level policy gates amber acceptance? Should enterprises get a toggle to accept amber auto-approvals?
- Explore machine-learned compatibility predictor using historical rollouts as a next-phase feature.

Appendix — example compatibility report (text):
Model: text-synth-7b v2.1
Regions evaluated: us-west1, us-east1, eu-central1
us-west1: score=92 (green) — native kernel v14, quant2-bit supported, p95 estimate +5%
us-east1: score=52 (amber) — quant profile mismatch (missing 2-bit fallback), kernel present but older; recommend 5% canary 48h
eu-central1: score=18 (red) — kernel missing, memory exceed on p3-small(legacy); block

Action: Block global strict pin. Recommend flexible pin scoped to us-west1 + canary to us-east1 while building eu-central variant.

Owner notes (Priya):
This doc is intentionally procedural rather than prescriptive — the goal is to provide a live checklist that we can automate into the registry UI and the /pins/validate API. Next steps: convert scoring into a microservice (INF-3248) and add the pre-pin audit widget to Platform Console.
